meta.title: Change the shared proxy settings today

security.label: Step with an evidenced pain point

nodes.label: Find the settings file
nodes.explanation: Ports, listeners and the stack directory hostname are machine settings in the [caddy] table of config.toml, found in DEVHOST_CONFIG_DIR, else XDG_CONFIG_HOME/devhost, else ~/.config/devhost. devhost caddy --help says only 'Download and trust it once, then start it before running a stack.'; no help text names config.toml, and devhost start never prints its path, which first appears in 'Applied the shared Caddy settings from <path>.' after the file was already edited. The privileged-ports help line reads 'Let Caddy listen on low ports without root (Linux)', although the command may download Caddy and runs sudo setcap; trust, one line below, says it asks for a password (proxy-settings-05).

sources.label: caddy help never mentions config.toml
privileged-ports help omits sudo and download
File path from two env vars, else HOME

nodes.label: Save [caddy] settings
nodes.explanation: The person changes httpsPort, http and httpPort, bindHost, stackDirectoryHost, stackDirectoryAllowRemote or adminAddress and saves the file. The browser config editor (flow config-editor: off by default, saves only from this machine) validates the same file and writes it; every running stack then applies it exactly like a save from an editor.

sources.label: Docs: the [caddy] keys and their defaults
Config editor validates, then writes the file

nodes.label: Every stack reads it
nodes.explanation: Each running stack watches config.toml with the manifest's debounce and applies one save at a time. It reads and validates the file: unknown keys, ports outside 1 to 65535, an empty adminAddress, an unsupported bindHost and a stackDirectoryHost with a scheme, port or path are each rejected by key. Any error from reading or applying the file comes back to this loop, which logs it as a rejection.

sources.label: Watch loop applies each save, logs errors
Validation names each bad key
Read the file, then apply it to Caddy

nodes.label: Render the Caddyfile
nodes.explanation: Under a lock every devhost process shares, Caddy's Caddyfile, routes, 404 site and stack directory site are rendered for the new settings; a directory hostname that a running stack claims fails here. bindHost becomes a default_bind directive, except on macOS, where 127.0.0.1 renders no directive whatever the port, so Caddy listens on every interface even on unprivileged ports such as the docs' httpsPort = 4443. Nothing at Caddy start, stack start or apply states the listener scope; only a docs bullet mentions it, giving a privileged-port reason that does not hold above port 1023, and devhost caddy privileged-ports on macOS prints that no setup is needed (proxy-settings-01).

sources.label: Render Caddyfile, routes, 404 and directory
macOS: no bind for 127.0.0.1 on any port
macOS: no privileged-port setup needed

nodes.label: Reload the shared Caddy
nodes.explanation: Caddy reloads through the admin address it runs, and devhost records the new settings in applied.json; when another stack already applied the same settings, nothing reloads twice. devhost never checks the ports itself and relies on Caddy's reload failing. On macOS a wildcard listener binds beside a program that holds the port on 127.0.0.1 only, so the save is reported applied while IPv4 requests reach that program and fail TLS and IPv6 requests reach Caddy; the docs promise a rejection for a held port (proxy-settings-02). A render or reload that fails re-renders the running settings, keeps Caddy on them and returns the error to the watch loop.

sources.label: Reload via admin API, then record applied
Docs: a port another program holds is rejected

nodes.label: Applied + same URLs
nodes.explanation: After Caddy moved, each stack whose settings changed publishes its state and prints 'Applied the shared Caddy settings from <path>.' and then every service URL again, whatever changed. URLs are built from httpsPort alone, so with http = true the plain-HTTP address a tunnel needs is never printed. A stackDirectoryHost change moves the directory to a URL printed nowhere while the old one answers 404, and turning on stackDirectoryAllowRemote prints the same lines with no word that stack URLs and raw configuration files are now readable from the network (proxy-settings-04). No devhost output names the directory URL at all (stack-directory-06, owned by stack-run-stop).

sources.label: Applied line, then every URL again
URLs from httpsPort only; no directory

nodes.label: Services keep running
nodes.explanation: Services, routes, terminals and chat sessions keep running, as the docs promise, and nothing reaches the services. A service is told DEVHOST_HOST and DEVHOST_PATH but never the public port or scheme, and service references offer no public URL, so with any httpsPort but 443 an app that builds https://$DEVHOST_HOST/ for an OAuth redirect, a CORS allowlist or an emailed link gets an address that does not answer. Hard-coding the port in the manifest's env stays wrong after a saved httpsPort change, which restarts nothing (proxy-settings-06).

sources.label: Env: host and path, never the public port
Docs: services keep running

nodes.label: Open pages show 0/N
nodes.explanation: Caddy moves before the stack publishes, so every page open on the old port loses its status stream at the reload. The toolbar draws every service down (0/N), as if all had crashed, and keeps reconnecting to the page's own origin, which no longer answers; minutes later it still names no new port and offers no link to the new URL. Only moving the port back recovers the page. The docs say every stack updates its URLs in devtools, which holds only for pages opened on the new port (proxy-settings-03; drawing any lost connection as an outage is owned by notices-and-feedback).

sources.label: Caddy moves before open pages are told
Disconnect: all down; retry the old origin
Every service marked failed

nodes.label: Settings rejected
nodes.sublabel: no word of what still runs
nodes.explanation: An invalid file, a directory hostname a running stack claims, or a reload Caddy refuses keeps Caddy on its running settings. Each stack prints 'shared Caddy settings rejected: <reason>' once and never says what keeps running; the toolbar calls it 'devhost config change not applied', a third name. The directory collision names only a PID, often of the stack printing it, while service collisions name the manifest. A later devhost start of a project that uses the reserved hostname is refused without naming config.toml, the key or the service. Fixing the file prints nothing, so every terminal still ends on the rejection (proxy-settings-04). When a refused save, or one made while Caddy was stopped, is applied later by another stack's start or by devhost caddy start, the stacks already running are not told: they keep this notice, and their toolbar links and printed URLs keep the old port while the stack directory lists the new one (proxy-settings-07).

sources.label: Rejection logged; a fix logs nothing
Toolbar: devhost config change not applied
Directory collision names only a PID

nodes.label: Reachable from the LAN
nodes.explanation: With no bind directive, every stack's pages, APIs and /__devhost__/ control routes answer requests through the Mac's network address, although the person asked for loopback only (proxy-settings-01). Chat trusts the Host and Origin headers any client can set, so another device can start a coding agent in the stack's checkout (network-exposure-01, owned by agent-chat; its stopgap admits only loopback clients). Only the stack directory checks the client address itself, unless stackDirectoryAllowRemote is set.

sources.label: Control guard checks Host and Origin only
Only the directory checks the client IP
Docs: macOS keeps all interfaces

cards.title: What already works
items: Every running stack watches config.toml and applies a save without restarting services, routes, terminals or chat sessions
Caddy moves in one reload under a lock every devhost process shares; settings another stack already applied are not reloaded twice
An invalid file, a claimed directory hostname or a refused reload keeps Caddy on the settings it runs, and the files are rendered back for them
Validation names each bad key: unknown keys, ports outside 1 to 65535, an unsupported bindHost, a hostname with a scheme or port
The stack directory refuses clients on other machines unless stackDirectoryAllowRemote is set; a repeated rejection is printed once

cards.title: Tickets on this journey
items: network-exposure-01 (owned by agent-chat) Anyone on the network can start a coding agent on a running stack; bindHost 127.0.0.1 does not close it on macOS
proxy-settings-01 On macOS bindHost = 127.0.0.1 is ignored even on unprivileged ports: every stack stays reachable from the network and devhost never says so
proxy-settings-02 On macOS a port another program holds on loopback is reported applied; IPv4 requests reach that program, IPv6 requests reach Caddy
proxy-settings-03 After an httpsPort change every open page is stranded on the old port with all services drawn down, and nothing names the new address
proxy-settings-04 A save prints only Applied and the same URLs; rejections never say what keeps running, collisions name a PID, and a fix prints nothing
proxy-settings-06 With any HTTPS port but 443 a service cannot learn its public URL, and a port change leaves hard-coded ones stale
stack-directory-06 (owned by stack-run-stop) No devhost output names the stack directory URL, so a stackDirectoryHost change moves it silently
proxy-settings-05 The CLI never says where ports and listeners are set; the privileged-ports help line omits its download and password prompt
proxy-settings-07 When a later start applies a config.toml change that a save could not, running stacks keep the old port's links and the 'not applied' notice

cards.title: Evidence
items: Traced from alexgorbatchev/devhost at edb5c0fc01cabae490e92ac23d4c785ec896c4ed; the review exercised build 0.0.12 live: httpsPort moves with two stacks running, stackDirectoryHost and stackDirectoryAllowRemote changes, an invalid port, a port held on loopback, a directory hostname collision, bindHost 127.0.0.1 from the LAN and a service's environment; privileged-ports was read from its help and code only. This diagram was traced from source only.
